I now have a complete picture. Let me compile the full implementation plan. --- ## Implementation Plan: Combined i18n + Accessibility Feature Branch for Tutors SvelteKit App --- ### Part 1: i18n Library Decision -- Custom Lightweight Rune-Based Approach **Recommendation: Custom lightweight i18n built on the existing `rune()` factory pattern.** Rationale against the alternatives: 1. **sveltekit-i18n** (from the old branch): It is store-based (`$t()`), uses Svelte 4 reactive syntax (`$:`, `on:click`), and the old integration relied on query-param locale switching with full page reloads via `window.location.href`. The library adds a dependency and its store-based API would be an alien pattern in a codebase that exclusively uses Svelte 5 runes. Converting its stores to work reactively alongside `$state`/`$derived` is possible but awkward. 2. **Paraglide.js**: Excellent for large apps requiring type-safe compiled messages, but it introduces a build step (compiler), message file format (`.json` in `messages/` with a specific structure), and a SvelteKit adapter. For approximately 90 strings across 25 files, this is over-engineered. It also handles routing via path-based locales (`/en/page`, `/fr/page`) which the app does not need and would conflict with the existing `(course-reader)/(home)/(live)` route groups. 3. **Custom rune-based approach**: The codebase already has the `rune()` factory in `$lib/runes.svelte` as the canonical state primitive. A custom i18n module that stores `locale` as a rune and exports a `t()` function using `$derived` is the natural fit. It introduces zero new dependencies, zero build steps, uses the same pattern as `currentCourse`, `tutorsId`, `animationDelay` etc., and handles ~90 strings with a tiny runtime footprint. Cookie persistence is straightforward to add in the server hook. The string count is modest enough that type safety from a compiler is not critical -- a TypeScript interface over the message keys provides sufficient safety. --- ### Part 2: Architecture Design #### 2.1 Locale State and Translation Function A new file `src/lib/services/i18n/index.ts` (or `.svelte.ts` if it needs `$state` directly; but since it uses the `rune()` factory, a plain `.ts` works just as other services do): ``` src/lib/services/i18n/ index.ts -- exports locale rune, t() function, setLocale(), SUPPORTED_LOCALES messages/ en.ts -- English messages (default) fr.ts -- French messages de.ts -- German messages it.ts -- Italian messages es.ts -- Spanish messages types.ts -- MessageKeys type (union of all dot-path keys) ``` The `locale` rune: `export const locale = rune("en");` The `t()` function: a simple getter that reads `locale.value`, indexes into the loaded messages object by dot-path key, and returns the string. Because it reads `locale.value`, any Svelte 5 `$derived` or template expression using `t("key")` will re-render when locale changes -- no stores, no page reload. Message format: flat dot-path keys, not nested objects. This is simpler to type-check and look up. Example: ```typescript // en.ts export default { "nav.search": "Search", "nav.search.exit": "Exit Search", "nav.search.tip": "Search this course", "nav.layout": "Layout", "nav.layout.options": "Layout Options", // ... "home.values.title": "The Values of the project", "home.developer.title": "Developer Experience", "home.developer.description": "The Developer Experience ...", // ... } as const; ``` The existing 5-locale translations from `origin/i18n_lgriffin_2024` will be ported by mapping their nested keys to flat dot-paths. The HTML content in values (like ``, ``) is preserved as-is -- the components already use `{@html}` for these. #### 2.2 Locale Persistence (Cookie-Based) - `src/hooks.server.ts`: Extend the existing `handle` to read a `locale` cookie from the request and inject it into `event.locals.locale`. On response, if the locale was changed (via a form action or API route), set the cookie. - `src/routes/+layout.server.ts`: Pass `locals.locale` to the client via the `load` return. - `src/routes/+layout.svelte`: Initialize `locale.value` from `data.locale` on mount. - Client-side locale switching: `setLocale("fr")` updates the rune AND sets `document.cookie`. No page reload. Since the rune is reactive, all `t()` calls re-evaluate. - Fallback chain: cookie -> `Accept-Language` header -> `"en"`. - The `` attribute in `app.html` becomes dynamic: the root layout sets `document.documentElement.lang = locale.value` in an `$effect`. #### 2.3 Language Switcher Component New component `src/lib/ui/components/LanguageSwitcher.svelte` using the existing `Menu` component (Skeleton Popover) for consistency. Placed in the `LayoutMenu` alongside theme/card/code style controls, under a "Language" section. Each language shown with its native name (English, Francais, Deutsch, Italiano, Espanol). Uses proper ARIA: the trigger button gets `aria-label="Change language"`, each option is a button with the language name. #### 2.4 String Organization Flat dot-path keys organized by domain (not by component or page), because many strings are shared across components: ``` nav.* -- Navigation bar strings (search, layout, info, toc, calendar, online) menu.* -- Profile menu strings (connect, disconnect, share presence, etc.) home.* -- Home page strings (info, links, welcome, values, credits) course.* -- Course reader strings (search page, visit card, live page) auth.* -- Authentication strings (sign in, terms) time.* -- Time/analytics table strings (headers, labels) content.* -- Content viewer strings (slide controls, calendar table) footer.* -- Footer strings (version, message, alt text) error.* -- Error page strings a11y.* -- ARIA labels and sr-only strings (skip nav, landmarks, etc.) ``` --- ### Part 3: Accessibility Fixes #### 3.1 Skip Navigation Link Add to `TutorsShell.svelte` as the very first child, before `
`: ```html {t("a11y.skipToContent")} ``` The `
` element gets `id="main-content"` and `tabindex="-1"`. #### 3.2 Landmark Roles and Labels - `MainNavigator.svelte`: Wrap `` in `
`. - `Breadcrumbs.svelte`: Wrap the outer div in `
`. The `
    ` already exists. - `SecondaryNavigator.svelte`: Wrap in `
    `. - `Sidebar.svelte`: Add `aria-label={t("a11y.sidebar")}` to the `Dialog.Content`. The Skeleton Dialog v4 already manages focus trap. - `Menu.svelte` (Popover): Add `aria-label` to `Popover.Content`. - `Footer.svelte`: The `
    ` tag is already in `TutorsShell.svelte`. Add `aria-label={t("a11y.footer")}`. #### 3.3 Focus Management on Route Change - `src/routes/(course-reader)/+layout.svelte`: In the existing `afterNavigate`, after scrolling, call `document.getElementById("main-content")?.focus()`. This moves focus to the main content area after SPA navigation, ensuring screen reader users do not get stranded on the previous page's content. - `src/lib/ui/learning-objects/content/Lab.svelte`: Same pattern in its `afterNavigate` -- focus the `#lab-panel` element after scroll. #### 3.4 `prefers-reduced-motion` Support - `src/lib/ui/navigators/animations.ts`: Export a `prefersReducedMotion` rune that reads `window.matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)")`. When true, all animation durations become 0 and start values become 1 (no scale/fly/slide). Modify `scaleTransition`, `slideFromLeft`, `slideFromRight` to be `$derived` from this. - `TutorsShell.svelte`: The `fly` and `slide` transitions on the header and footer should check `prefersReducedMotion.value` and use `duration: 0` when true. - `CourseVisitCard.svelte`: The `scale` transition should respect reduced motion. - `Cards.svelte`: Same for its `scale` transition. - `Context.svelte`: Same for its `fly` transitions. - Implementation: Create a helper `src/lib/services/a11y/reduced-motion.svelte.ts` that exports a reactive boolean. Import it in `animations.ts` to conditionally zero out durations. This keeps the change localized. #### 3.5 ARIA Labels for Interactive Elements - All `Icon` components with `tip` props already render tooltips but lack `aria-label`. The `Icon.svelte` component should propagate the `tip` value as `aria-label` on the wrapping element when there is no visible text. - `SearchButton.svelte`: Button needs `aria-label={isSearching ? t("nav.search.exit") : t("nav.search")}`. - `CalendarButton.svelte`: Button needs `aria-label={t("nav.calendar.tip")}`. - `TocButton.svelte`: Needs `aria-label={t("nav.toc.tip")}`. - `InfoButton.svelte`: Needs `aria-label={t("nav.info.tip")}`. - `CourseSentimentButton.svelte`: Already has `aria-label` -- update to use `t()`. - `CalendarHeatmap.svelte`: Already has `aria-label` -- update to use `t()`. - `Video.svelte`: The `aria-label="media embed code"` on the VIMP iframe should use `t()`. #### 3.6 Image Alt Text - `Footer.svelte`: `alt="sponsors"` should become `alt={t("footer.sponsorsAlt")}`. - `SetuIcon.svelte`: `alt="South East Technological University"` should use `t()`. - `TutorsTitle.svelte`: `alt={title}` is fine (dynamic). - `ConnectedProfile.svelte`: `alt={tutorsId.value?.name}` is fine (dynamic). #### 3.7 `sr-only` Usage - Add screen-reader-only text where icon-only buttons exist without labels: - `LayoutMenu.svelte` segmented control items (dark/light, portrait/circular/landscape, compacted/expanded) -- each `SegmentedControl.ItemText` currently only has an icon. Add `{t("nav.layout.dark")}` etc. - `CourseVisitCard.svelte` star/unstar button: Add `{courseVisit.favourite ? t("course.unstar") : t("course.star")}`. #### 3.8 `` Dynamic Update In `src/routes/+layout.svelte`, add an `$effect` that sets `document.documentElement.lang = locale.value` whenever locale changes. The initial value in `app.html` (`lang="en"`) serves as the SSR default. --- ### Part 4: Phased Implementation #### Phase 1: Infrastructure (3 files, no visible changes) **Goal**: Set up i18n and a11y infrastructure without changing any existing components. Files to create/modify: 1. **Create `src/lib/services/i18n/types.ts`** -- Define `SupportedLocale` type, `MessageMap` interface 2. **Create `src/lib/services/i18n/messages/en.ts`** -- All ~90 English strings as flat dot-path keys 3. **Create `src/lib/services/i18n/index.ts`** -- `locale` rune, `t()` function, `setLocale()`, `SUPPORTED_LOCALES` 4. **Create `src/lib/services/a11y/reduced-motion.svelte.ts`** -- `prefersReducedMotion` rune with matchMedia listener 5. **Modify `src/lib/runes.svelte.ts`** -- Export `locale` rune (or re-export from i18n service -- either works but keeping it in runes.svelte.ts follows the existing pattern for app-wide state) Testing: Import `t()` in one component to verify it resolves without errors. No visible UI change yet. #### Phase 2: App Shell a11y + Skip Nav + Focus Management (5 files) **Goal**: Core accessibility wins that are valuable even without i18n strings. Files to modify: 1. **`src/lib/ui/TutorsShell.svelte`** -- Add skip-nav link, `id="main-content"` on `
    `, `tabindex="-1"`, `aria-label` on footer. Wire up `prefers-reduced-motion` for fly/slide transitions. 2. **`src/lib/ui/navigators/MainNavigator.svelte`** -- Wrap in `
    `. 3. **`src/lib/ui/navigators/buttons/Breadcrumbs.svelte`** -- Wrap in `

Converting its stores to work reactively alongside `$state`/`$derived` is possible but awkward. 2. **Paraglide.js**: Excellent for large apps requiring type-safe compiled messages, but it introduces a build step (compiler), message file format (`.json` in `messages/` with a specific structure), and a SvelteKit adapter. For approximately 90 strings across 25 files, this is over-engineered. It also handles routing via path-based locales (`/en/page`, `/fr/page`) which the app does not need and would conflict with the existing `(course-reader)/(home)/(live)` route groups. 3. **Custom rune-based approach**: The codebase already has the `rune()` factory in `$lib/runes.svelte` as the canonical state primitive. A custom i18n module that stores `locale` as a rune and exports a `t()` function using `$derived` is the natural fit. It introduces zero new dependencies, zero build steps, uses the same pattern as `currentCourse`, `tutorsId`, `animationDelay` etc., and handles ~90 strings with a tiny runtime footprint. Cookie persistence is straightforward to add in the server hook. The string count is modest enough that type safety from a compiler is not critical -- a TypeScript interface over the message keys provides sufficient safety. --- ### Part 2: Architecture Design #### 2.1 Locale State and Translation Function A new file `src/lib/services/i18n/index.ts` (or `.svelte.ts` if it needs `$state` directly; but since it uses the `rune()` factory, a plain `.ts` works just as other services do): ``` src/lib/services/i18n/ index.ts -- exports locale rune, t() function, setLocale(), SUPPORTED_LOCALES messages/ en.ts -- English messages (default) fr.ts -- French messages de.ts -- German messages it.ts -- Italian messages es.ts -- Spanish messages types.ts -- MessageKeys type (union of all dot-path keys) ``` The `locale` rune: `export const locale = rune("en");` The `t()` function: a simple getter that reads `locale.value`, indexes into the loaded messages object by dot-path key, and returns the string. Because it reads `locale.value`, any Svelte 5 `$derived` or template expression using `t("key")` will re-render when locale changes -- no stores, no page reload. Message format: flat dot-path keys, not nested objects. This is simpler to type-check and look up. "home.values.title": "The Values of the project", "home.developer.title": "Developer Experience", "home.developer.description": "The Developer Experience ...", // ... } as const; ``` The existing 5-locale translations from `origin/i18n_lgriffin_2024` will be ported by mapping their nested keys to flat dot-paths. import en from "./messages/en"; import fr from "./messages/fr"; // ... export const SUPPORTED_LOCALES = ["en", "fr", "de", "it", "es"] as const; export type SupportedLocale = (typeof SUPPORTED_LOCALES)[number]; export type MessageKey = keyof typeof en; const messages: Record> = { en, fr, de, it, es }; export const locale = rune("en"); export function t(key: MessageKey): string { return messages[locale.value]?.[key] ?? messages.en[key] ?? key; } export function setLocale(newLocale: SupportedLocale) { locale.value = newLocale; if (typeof document !== "undefined") { document.cookie = `locale=${newLocale};path=/;max-age=31536000;SameSite=Lax`; document.documentElement.lang = newLocale; } } ``` Because `t()` reads `locale.value`, and `locale` is a rune wrapping `$state`, any Svelte 5 template expression `{t("key")}` is automatically reactive. When `setLocale` is called, every component re-renders with the new language. No page reload needed. **2. Why flat keys, not nested:** - Simpler TypeScript: `keyof typeof en` gives type safety on all keys directly. - No runtime dot-path splitting/traversal. - No ambiguity between `t("nav.search")` meaning `messages.nav.search` vs `messages["nav.search"]`. - The old branch used nested JSON; converting to flat TS objects is straightforward. **3. HTML in translations:** Some values/credits strings contain ``, `` with Tailwind classes. These are rendered with `{@html t("key")}`. This is already the pattern in the codebase (e.g., `{@html currentCourse?.value?.contentHtml}`). No special sanitization needed since all translation files are developer-authored, not user input. **4. Terms of service handling:** The `TutorsTerms.svelte` component contains a long markdown block. Rather than putting this in the flat message map (which would be unwieldy), create separate markdown files per locale (`src/lib/services/i18n/content/terms.en.md`, etc.) and dynamically import based on locale. Or, if simplicity is preferred, keep the full text as a message value -- it works but makes the message file large. **5. Cookie vs localStorage:** Cookie is chosen because: (a) it is readable on the server in `hooks.server.ts`, enabling SSR with the correct locale and setting `` correctly before hydration; (b) it persists across sessions; (c) it does not require JavaScript to be available for initial locale detection. localStorage cannot be read server-side. **6. Skeleton v4 Dialog/Popover focus management:** Skeleton v4 Dialog already provides focus trapping. No custom focus trap code needed. The `Sidebar.svelte` component using Dialog is already accessible for focus -- it just needs `aria-label` added to `Dialog.Content`. Similarly, Skeleton Popover manages focus correctly. --- ### Part 6: Risk Mitigation 1. **SSR hydration mismatch**: Since the server reads the cookie and passes `locale` via `load()`, and the client initializes from the same value, there should be no mismatch. The `` in `app.html` is `"en"` as the SSR default; the `$effect` in the root layout corrects it immediately on hydration. 2. **Performance**: All translations are statically imported TypeScript objects -- no async loading, no waterfall. The total message payload for 5 locales with ~90 keys each is approximately 15-20KB uncompressed, negligible after gzip. Tree-shaking will not eliminate unused locales since they are dynamically indexed, but this is acceptable given the small size. 3. **Missing translations**: The `t()` function falls back to English, then to the raw key. This means partially translated locales degrade gracefully to English rather than showing raw keys. 4. **Svelte 5 compatibility**: The entire approach uses only `$state` (via `rune()`), `$derived`, and `$effect` -- all Svelte 5 runes. No stores, no Svelte 4 syntax. 5. **Existing a11y ignore**: The single `` in `Breadcrumbs.svelte` (line 48) covers a `` with `onmouseenter`/`onmouseleave` for text truncation.
